text:
hey all, Heramb here (most people call me *Vansh*). I’ve done cloud cost FinOps work, I’m comfortable with Go, and I’ve spent time on data pipelines. I’m not looking for a warm-up task. I want to work on something real in olake-go, and I’m confident I can handle it.

Could you *guide* me on the following?

Which open olake-go issues are unassigned right now? CDC and incremental sync are where I want to go.
Is the PostgreSQL primary key update bug osamu described (old row stays in the destination) taken? If not, I’d like to pick it up.
Do bounty issues need a maintainer to assign them, or can I grab one and start?
Is there a design doc for the driver and writer layers? If not, which files should I read first before opening a PR?
How do I get an issue assigned to me? Should I comment on it first and wait, or is there a process I should follow? Also, should I ask here before opening a new issue, or go ahead and raise it?

Point me to whatever you think I should take next.

text: Hey, you will have to start with good first issues. this is what is recommended for the first time contributors. the bounty issues are only provided to the contributors that have done significant amount of contributions (5-6) and are familiar with the code base. to get the issue assigned to you just comment on that issue, if we believe the issue is of lower priority we will redirect you to better issues. this doc will help you with how to raise a PR and what all instructions needs to be followed: <https://olake.io/docs/community/issues-and-prs/|olake.io/docs/community/issues-and-prs>

text:
Hi! I’m a new contributor. I noticed AddConstantToInterface and SplitAndTrim
in utils/utils.go have no unit tests. I’ve written table-driven tests for
them following the style in utils_test.go (all passing locally). Would a PR
adding these be welcome? Also, in types/set.go, Hash() returns “false” when
hashstructure.Hash fails (there’s an unfinished TODO), so failing elements
would share the same key. How would you prefer that to be handled?
